history.reason: BitOp and its four variants moved from kevy-embedded to kevy-store, where the byte arithmetic they name now lives so both surfaces can call one implementation. kevy-embedded/without-example fell 170 -> 165 by exactly those items; kevy-store/without-example rose 285 -> 289, four rather than five because the enum itself gained an executable example. The deficit is one item smaller overall; the ratchet is keyed per crate, so a move between crates shows as growth in the receiving key. bitop_combine and Route::BitOpStore both carry examples that teach — the padding rules and the 0xff tail of NOT, and why BITOP cannot ride Route::Single(1).

kevy-resp/without-example 107→118: eighteen public items in the fuzz module left the docs-owed set (the crate's own #![allow(missing_docs)] had been hiding them) and joined the examples-owed one, which is what documenting them costs. Seven now carry a runnable example; the remaining eleven are struct and enum-variant fields, which cannot carry a doctest at all. The deficit as a whole fell — 2549 regions to 2536 — and docs owed went to zero.

The tiering INFO gained its compression terms: kevy-vlog's CompressionStats and kevy-embedded's KevyTierCompression each carry four public fields (raw, payload, frame header, dictionary bytes), and rustdoc counts a field as an item that has no example. The struct and the methods that return them all carry executable examples (Vlog::compression, KevyTierCompression, Store::tier_compression); only the eight fields are new growth, four per crate.

kevy-verbs is new: the single-shard command layer the server and the embedded engine share. Every function, the Verb type, the VERBS table and the args, reply, aof and cmd modules carry executable examples. The 16 counted here are items rustdoc reports but no example can hang off: the five reply-wording constants, the six public fields of ScanOpts and Verb, and the five variants of Effect.
